Escape the tax man! In the UK if you want to invest beyond 20k in equities per year open a standard investment account alongside an ISA. Put all your high growth stocks - individual picks and ETF's - within the ISA. Therefore if the market dips you don't need to sell and if it races you won't pay any tax on your profits.  Then go with a steady eddy fundamental like a global ETF in your investment account. Sell this by 5 April each financial year to realise your profits (hopefully) and if the amount invested is circa 20k your gain should sit below the 3k capital gains tax you are allowed tax free. Dividends may be close to the £500 mark however - you pay tax beyond this. It's best using a distribution fund for this and do not reinvest dividends during the year - this provides an audit trail should HMRC come calling. Of course this only works if you aren't using your CGT allowance elsewhere and remember all sales during the financial year count towards your allowance. And you only get to use 3k in that year, it's not carried forward. If the investment is down don't sell. This way you invest around 40k tax free per annum. Not financial advice, just a useful tip 😊
